result.title: FORK: Co-Evolving Safe Disclosure and Decision Skills Against Attackers Who Read Every Refusal
result.summary: When a guardrail rejects an LLM agent's action, its message reaches any attacker observing the trajectory: a fixed refusal leaves benign users unable to recover, whereas an explanation can tell the attacker what to try next. We study this as safe disclosure: explaining rejections so that authorized tasks recover without increasing adaptive attack success. Safe disclosure depends on both the decision and the message: what the guardrail blocks and what it reveals to the agent and the attacker. Because hand-written rules alone cannot anticipate how adaptive attackers probe decisions or use messages, we introduce FORK, which co-evolves a guardrail's natural-language decision and disclosure skills with an attacker that reads every public message. Each exploited message and permissive decision gives FORK evidence for a gradient-free revision of its natural-language skill library. We evaluate FORK on four benchmarks. Averaged over three agents on FORK-World, FORK cuts attack success rate (ASR) under adaptive attack from 78.4% to 14.1% and keeps utility above 85%, outperforming baselines on both ASR and utility. Notably, on MT-AgentRisk, whose environments and tasks are unseen in training, FORK lowers ASR from 70.6% to 9.1% with 93.1% benign utility.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 LLM agent 护栏拒绝时的「安全披露」问题：拒绝消息既要让正常用户能恢复任务，又不能给自适应攻击者提供试探线索；为此提出 FORK，让护栏的自然语言决策与披露技能同「读取全部公开消息」的攻击者共同进化，并在四个基准上降低攻击成功率、同时保持效用。
AI.relevance_reason: 「对外披露多少中间信息」的权衡与用自适应探测来评价泄漏的做法，可能为 LVR 中外露 latent 推理内容或停止/拒绝理由时的信息泄漏风险评价提供概念线索，可核查其评价方式是否适用于推理轨迹披露场景。
